Date of Hearing & Delivery of Judgment: 17.07.2017.

 

 

 

 

 

 J U D G M E N T [O R A L] 

 

 

 

 U.B. Saha,J,
The instant appeal is filed by the appellant, Sri Sujan Shil, Proprietor of Sri Sri Laxmi Stores, P.O. Usha Bazaar, P.S. Airport P.S., Agartala, West Tripura under
Section 15
of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 challenging the judgment dated 03.05.2017 passed by the Ld. District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum (hereinafter referred to as District Forum), West Tripura, Agartala in case No. C.C. 18 of 2017 whereby and whereunder the Ld. District Forum directed the appellant (hereinafter referred to as opposite party) to pay the price of the mobile phone Rs.9,500/- to the respondent (hereinafter referred to as petitioner) for purchasing a new one and to pay Rs.10,000/- for deficiency of service, in total Rs.19,500/-. Petitioner is to give back damaged mobile to the opposite party, if it is under her custody. Payment is to be made within one month, if it is not paid, it will carry interest @ 9% per annum.
Heard Mr. Kanu Lal Das, Ld. Counsel appearing for the appellant-opposite party as well as Mr. Sumit Debnath, Ld. Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent-petitioner.
 Brief facts needed to be discussed are as follows:-
The petitioner, Miss Madhurima Dey had purchased one mobile phone OPPO NEO-7 on payment of Rs.9,500/-. A warranty card dated 19.10.2016 bearing IMEI1:861227039811515 and Black IMEI2:861227039811507 was given by the opposite party in the name of complainant against purchase of the said phone and it was said that warranty period would be for one year from the date of purchase of the said mobile phone. After few days of purchase, the mobile was not working and accordingly, she went to the opposite party on 23.11.2016 after 33 days. The phone was charged for 24 hours and the same was handed over to the opposite party, but it was not in working condition. Again, she visited the shop of the opposite party. The opposite party, Proprietor of Sri Sri Laxmi Stores stated that the mobile is to be sent to Guwahati for repairing for which the opposite party kept the said phone with him without providing any receipt and he also told that the phone has to be sent to the Service Centre for repairing as it was within the warranty period. After a week when the petitioner visited the said shop of the opposite party, the petitioner was informed that the repair was under process and it would take some time. Again after about 15 days, she along with her mother visited the shop of the opposite party. On 30.12.2016, the opposite party returned the said phone stating that Rs.3,000/- would be required for repairing of the said mobile as the mobile phone was damaged due to immersion in water. The mobile was ultimately handed over to the petitioner after a month. Thereafter, she served a lawyer notice to the opposite party and finally lodged a complaint petition before the Ld. District Forum claiming of Rs.50,000/- as compensation.
Opposite party appeared and filed written statement denying the claim. It is stated that the mobile phone in question was purchased by the father of the petitioner in her name and accordingly, the opposite party issued cash memo in the name of the petitioner for the mobile. Thereafter, opposite party along with father of the petitioner went to the Authorized Service Centre, namely, Pacetel Systems Private Ltd. at Shanti Para, Agartala wherein the said mobile phone was inspected by the authorized service centre and found that the mobile was damaged due to immersion in the water and it can only be repaired on payment of Rs.2,700/-. It is further stated that the complaint petition was not maintainable being the Company who manufactured the said mobile was not made party and there was no deficiency in service by the opposite party being seller.
Petitioner produced the cash memo, notice, warranty card of the mobile phone and also submitted her statement on affidavit and the statement on affidavit of her father Sri Manik Chandra Dey.
On the other hand, the opposite party produced reply to demand notice, postal receipt, copy of opinion/report of Sri Tapas Roy of Pacetel Systems Private Ltd. dated 27.12.2016, three photographs of the mobile set. Opposite party, Sri Sujan Shil also submitted his statement on affidavit.
The Ld. District Forum considering the documents exhibited and also the evidence on record passed the impugned judgment.
Mr. Das, Ld. Counsel while urging for setting aside the impugned judgment would submit that the Ld. District Forum passed the impugned judgment on mere presumption without examining any expert witness like the technician from the authorized service centre though on 03.04.2017, an application was filed by the opposite party for examining Sri Tapas Roy of Pacetel Systems Private Ltd. who had examined the mobile and submitted report. He further submits that the opposite party is not liable for non-functioning of the mobile phone even within the warranty period, as the mobile was not functioning due to immersion in the water. He has again contended that the petitioner did not make out any case that there was any manufacturing defect in the mobile. He has finally contended that the petitioner alleges a defect in the mobile, which cannot be determined without proper analysis or test of the mobile. The District Forum shall obtain a sample of the goods/mobile from the complainant, seal it and authenticate it in the manner prescribed and refer the sample so sealed to the appropriate laboratory along with a direction that such laboratory make an analysis or test, whichever may be necessary, with a view to finding out whether such mobile suffer from any defect alleged in the complaint or from any other defect and to report its findings thereon to the District Forum within a period of forty-five days of the receipt of the reference or within such extended period as may be granted by the District Forum, but in the instant case, the District Forum neither obtained the alleged defective mobile, nor examined the same by the appropriate authority for which itself the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside.
In support of his aforesaid contention, he has relied upon a judgment dated of the Hon'ble Apex Court dated 05.05.1999 in
M.R.F. Ltd Vs Jagdish Lal and Anr.
in Appeal (Civil) 2710 of 1999, [1999 (2) SCR 1089].
He has also submitted a judgment dated 23 February, 2012 of Hon'ble State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Chennai in F.A./8/2011 (
The Associate Tractor Branch ... Vs Solomon, 127-B, Antoniar
), wherein the Hon'ble State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Chennai held that "if manufacturing defect is alleged either directly or impliedly, the burden is upon the complainant, to prove the same." And the District Forum
in that case
has given a finding, "that the defects in the tyres had happened due to manufacturing, by the Tyre Company, then the District Forum should have given a direction against the Tyre Company, impleading them as a party, which was not done, whereas a dealer who has not given any warranty, was penalized, by the District Forum, which finding, are unable to concur."
Per contra Mr. Debnath, Ld. Counsel appearing for the petitioner while supporting the impugned judgment would contend that the Ld. District Forum rightly passed the impugned judgment, as the opposite party being the seller has the responsibility either to repair or to change the mobile within the warranty period. He further submits that the seller is duty bound to disclose the details of service centre and manufacturer to the customer and non-disclosure of the details is itself an unfair trade practice. He also submits that from the evidence of the petitioner it is found that the mobile was not working for switch problem and the opposite party initially said that the mobile was sent to Guwahati, but later on it was stated that the mobile was not sent to Guwahati and they claimed Rs.3,000/- on the ground that the mobile was immersion in the water. He finally submits that it is not necessary to make the manufacturer of the mobile party being the opposite party is the Dealer of the Manufacturing Company.
We have gone through the impugned judgment as well as the order sheet of the District Forum and evidence on record and also the judgment cited by the Ld. Counsel for the appellant. It appears from record that the opposite party to prove his case submitted an application on 03.04.2017 for calling one Sri Tapas Roy of Pacetel Systems Private Ltd. as one of the witness in support of his case as Sri Tapas Roy inspected the alleged defective mobile and found that the water has damaged inside the mobile. It further appears from record that the report of Sri Tapas Roy was also placed before the Ld. District Forum, but on 03.04.2017 the Ld. District Forum passed the following orders:-
Petition has been filed on behalf of the complainant praying for time on the ground of illness of the Counsel. Examination-in-Chief filed by the O.P. (Sri Sujan Shil) along with 04 documents submitted by Firisti. Another petition filed by the O.P. praying for issuance of summon upon Sri Tapas Roy. The President is out of station. Case is adjourned. To 12.04.2017 for cross examination of the O.P.W." Thereafter, on 12.04.2017:-O.P.W. was cross-examined and the matter was fixed for argument on 26.04.2017. On 26.04.2017:- Both the parties appeared through their Ld. Counsel and written argument was filed by the petitioner and also argument was made by the Ld. Counsel for the O.P. and finally on 03.05.2017 passed the impugned judgment. From the aforesaid facts it is crystal clear that the District Forum neither issued any summon to Sri Tapas Roy of Pacetel Systems Pvt. Ltd., Authorised Service Centre, nor disposed of the said application dated 03.04.2017 filed by the O.P., more so, the District Forum very generously has come to the conclusion, as if, no law is applicable to the parties and there is no burden upon the complainant to prove the manufacturing defect of the mobile directing the opposite parties to pay the value of the mobile and also to pay Rs.10,000/-, in total Rs.19,500/- for deficiency of service and price of the mobile phone with interest @9% per annum, if the payment is not made within one month only on the basis of the statement of witnesses and the documents placed before the Forum. Neither the District Forum, nor this Commission has expertisation as to whether the alleged defect in the mobile is a manufacturing defect or the defect was due to that the mobile was immerged in the water. Thus, according to us, the mobile should be sent to an expert by the District Forum on submission of the same by the petitioner or the District Forum may call the technician/expert who examined/inspected the mobile in the service centre. When an application is filed by the opposite party for examining a witness in support of their case, the District Forum is supposed to dispose of the said application and also to call the witness named in the application for the interest of justice. A party in a proceeding cannot be denied justice without providing any opportunity to prove its case.
In view of the above, the impugned judgment is set aside and the matter is remanded back to the Ld. District Forum to decide the case afresh, disposing of the application dated 03.04.2017 and also to call Sri Tapas Roy as O.P.W. and also to consider as to whether the Company who manufactured the mobile is a necessary party or not as raised by the opposite party in their written statement.
In the result, the appeal is partly allowed. No order as to costs.
Office is directed to release the statutory deposit as deposited by the appellant on submission of proper application.
Send down the records to the Ld. District Forum, West Tripura, Agartala.
